note: Canonical Wikidata identifiers for names and events in the checked Austria collection. Resolved by hand on 2026-11-17: a name is linked only when the candidate item's own description and dates fit the event it is named for; never by name alone. Ambiguous or unmatched names stay unlinked, with the reason.

Carl von Ghega.evidence: Wikidata: 'Austrian railway designer (1802–1860)'; named for the Semmering line, 1848–1854.

Karl Renner.evidence: Wikidata: 'first President of Austria (1870–1950)'; named for German-Austria, 1918, and Saint-Germain, 1919.

Klemens von Metternich.evidence: Wikidata: 'Austrian diplomat, foreign minister and Chancellor (1773–1859)'; named for the March 1848 uprising.

Alfred I. zu Windisch-Graetz.evidence: Wikidata: 'Alfred I, Prince of Windisch-Grätz, Austrian marshall (1787–1862)'; named for October 1848.

Franz Joseph I.evidence: Wikidata: 'Emperor of Austria and King of Hungary (1830–1916)'; named for 1857 and 1867. Other candidates of the same name lived in the 18th century.

Helmuth von Moltke.evidence: Wikidata: 'Helmuth von Moltke the Elder, German Field Marshal (1800–1891)'; named for Königgrätz, 1866. The Younger (1848–1916) was a child then.

Ferenc Deák.evidence: Wikidata: 'Hungarian politician (1803–1876)'; named for the Compromise of 1867. Other candidates are a researcher and a writer.

Victor Adler.evidence: Wikidata: 'foreign minister of Austria, editor (1852–1918)'; named for the Linz Program, 1882.

Gavrilo Princip.evidence: Wikidata: 'Bosnian Serb assassin (1894–1918)'; named for Sarajevo, 1914.

Charles I.evidence: Wikidata: 'Charles I of Austria, last monarch of Austria-Hungary (r. 1916–1918)'; named for the end of the monarchy in 1918. The name alone also matches Charles I of England, so it was resolved by this event.

Max Reinhardt.evidence: Wikidata: 'Austrian-American theater director and actor (1873–1943)'; named for the Salzburg Festival, 1920.

Hugo von Hofmannsthal.evidence: Wikidata: 'Austrian novelist, librettist, poet, dramatist (1874–1929)'; named for the Salzburg Festival, 1920.

Alexander Moissi.evidence: Wikidata: 'Albanian-born Austrian actor (1879–1935)'; named for the Salzburg Festival, 1920.

unresolved.Theodor von Latour: No Wikidata item found under this name; left unlinked.
unresolved.Franz Ferdinand: The top match is a rock band, and the archduke's candidate item showed inconsistent dates when checked; left unlinked until resolved.
